commits.message:
Let the acceptance settlement drill outwait and recognise a settlement

The acceptance arms kill-node-on-settlement before the withdrawals phase
submits its orders and gave it 1200 s. On the devnet profile a withdrawal's
settlement starts no sooner than the event wait (300 s) and block maturity
(900 s) after its order, so the wait always ended first: on a live stack
the first settlement transaction appeared 1348 s after arming. The wait is
now the profile's event wait and block maturity plus 25 minutes.

The trigger also listed two details the node stopped reporting in
bc56f0822, and not the one it reports while a settlement transaction is in
a block short of confirmation depth. Four of eleven settlement
transactions on that stack went from checkpointed to landed with no
journaled report between. The node's two wordings now live in
settlement.attempt-detail.ts, and the catalogue test builds its status
bodies from them, so a reworded detail fails the test.

Red before the fix (tests/devnet-stack-chaos.test.ts, 6 passed, 2 failed):
  recognises each targeted moment from the node's status bodies
    expected [ ...(2) ] to deeply equal [ ...(2) ]
    (the landed detail, false against true)
  lets the acceptance wait past the earliest a withdrawal's settlement can
  start
    expected 1200000 to be greater than 1200000

Name files and tests for what they do, and delete one-time goal scripts

- Files, constants and Aiken test modules named after an issue, goal
  or phase label are named for their purpose. Markdown docs, skills
  and the remaining code comments state the rule instead of citing a
  label. Decision records keep their identifiers.
- The node creates the follower's tables in the same transaction as
  the rest of its schema, so they are always present: the
  `landed_block_follower_schema_missing` hold and the table probes
  behind it are gone. The commit test fakes share one helper that
  models a complete, empty database.
- One-time capture and benchmark scripts with no caller are gone: the
  phase4 environment and slot-config captures, the phase1 query-write
  and group-commit benchmarks, the chunk128 candidate bench entry and
  the 10k smoke entry, whose test runs in the joined DA suite.
- The retained-DA boundary corpus check is
  `test:retained-da-boundary-corpus`.
- Naming guide: labels go in commit messages and decision records,
  never in names, comments, test titles or messages.

Give the devnet node read budgets the acceptance drills fit in

An armed acceptance phase drill reads its trigger every 10 ms. The devnet
node ran with the public rate limits (10 reads and 5 health reads a second
for one client), and the controller, its drills and the CLIs are one
loopback client. The node therefore refused most of the drill's reads and
the journey's own: /tx-status answered 429 with a JSON body, which the
journey read as "not committed yet".

Seen on a fresh devnet stack (campaign acceptance-user-cli-2, 2026-11-25):
the node committed transfers T1-T3 and their block landed six seconds after
they were submitted, yet the journey reported "still waiting for L2 tx ...
to be committed (node ready)" for 19 minutes, and kill-node-on-admission
ended with 'trigger "durable admission backlog > 0" did not hold within
1200 s'. The backlog was above zero for 37 ms. On that stack, 60 reads of
/pipeline-status in a row got 30 answers and then 429s, and /tx-status
answered 429 with them. The 10 ms interval dates from 2026-10-04; the rate
limits from 2026-10-26.

- The devnet node's environment raises the read and health budgets
  (HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_READ, HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_HEALTH). Every other class keeps
  its default.
- The journey treats a 429 as an unanswered read and names it in its
  reports, like a 5xx, instead of reading the refusal's body as a status.
- The interval has a name, ACCEPTANCE_TRIGGER_POLL_MS, which the test
  compares the budgets with.

Tests, both red before the fix:
- the node's own reading of the devnet listen environment must allow more
  reads a second than the drills make, for read (client and global) and
  health;
- a wait whose reads are refused with 429 must name the refusal when it
  times out.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-l1-origin.test.ts: 13 passed, 1 failed before; 14
  passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-journey-robustness.test.ts: 22 passed, 1 failed
  before; 23 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related on the four changed
  sources: 777 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped in 72 files (the
  deployment-profile skips).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on the changed
  files; module-size ceilings.

Not verified:
- No passing acceptance run on a devnet stack yet. Whether 10 ms reads
  catch the 37 ms admission moment every time is not shown.

Delete the code that carried older database shapes, and the remaining labels

Every store is created whole from one schema, so nothing can hold a
row or a journal of an older shape.

- Withdrawal outref: every insert writes `decoded` or `undecodable`.
  The `unknown` state, its two indexes, the bounded backfill and the
  `E_PUBLIC_READ_MIGRATING` read refusal are gone.
- Availability operation journal: opening creates schema 3 or refuses
  another version. The in-place upgrade and its halt-cleared event are
  gone.
- Transaction fuzz: the reference leg runs on scripts naming the BLS
  builtins it used to skip, with no divergence, so the
  `blsTagNumbering` class and its pins are gone.
- The data-breadth wrapper script is gone; its seven tests run in the
  ordinary validation suite.
- Comments, test titles and messages state the rule instead of citing
  an issue number, goal label or ruling label.

Keep the tool when the acceptance journey attempts a submission

AcceptanceJourney overrides attempt to refuse work after cancellation. The
override still had the four parameters attempt had before 6e43bd7ed added
the tool, so it called the journey's attempt without it and every deposit
and withdrawal under acceptance defaulted to the node CLI. With the runner
fixed in the previous commit, an acceptance run on a fresh devnet stack
still stopped at deposits-concurrent with "error: unknown command
'deposit'" (campaign acceptance-user-cli-1, 2026-11-24).

The override now forwards whatever the journey's attempt takes, so a later
parameter cannot be dropped the same way.

Test: a deposit made through an AcceptanceJourney must reach the CLI runner
as the user tool. Before the fix it failed with "expected [ [ 'node',
'deposit' ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 'user', 'deposit' ] ]". The plain
journey's equivalent assertion never constructs the acceptance subclass.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-acceptance.test.ts: 18 passed, 1 failed before the
  fix; with tests/devnet-stack-acceptance-process.test.ts, 23 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related
  src/devnet-stack/acceptance-journey.ts: 775 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped
  in 72 files (the same deployment-profile skips as before).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on both files.

Not verified:
- No passing acceptance run on a devnet stack yet.

Run acceptance deposits and withdrawals through midgard-user

6e43bd7ed moved deposits and withdrawals to midgard-user and taught the
journey's own runner to honour a request's tool. The acceptance runner kept
its own copy of the launch and always ran the node CLI, so acceptance stopped
at its first journey phase with "error: unknown command 'deposit'".

Both runners now take the program, directory and environment from one
helper, cliProcess, and the run key from journeyRunKey; each keeps only its
own way of executing the process.

Test: a request naming the user tool, run through the acceptance runner
against stub CLIs, must start dist/cli.js in the user CLI package with the
user environment, the user's seed and the submission markers, and none of the
operator's secrets. Before the fix it failed with "expected 'node CLI' to be
'midgard-user'". A request naming no tool still runs the node CLI. It sits
beside the acceptance process tests because no existing test runs a request
through this runner.

Verified (run here):
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --file
  tests/devnet-stack-acceptance-process.test.ts: 3 passed, 1 failed before
  the fix; 4 passed after.
- contrib test --package midgard-node-tools --related on the three changed
  sources: 774 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped in 72 files (the skips are
  deployment-profile conditions in devnet-stack-watcher and
  devnet-stack-service-preflight).
- tsc --noEmit in midgard-node-tools; eslint and prettier on the four files.

Not verified:
- No acceptance run on a devnet stack.

Close a node worker's L1 node transport before its thread ends

A sidecar is a child of the thread that spawned it, and only that thread
collects its exit. The commit worker and the settlement worker open the
shared L1 node transport and never closed it: the node's L1 access closes
only its fact store. The commit worker's parent terminates the thread on its
output, once per commit tick, so every run left one defunct
midgard-l1-node-transport child of the node (425 after 65 minutes of a
local devnet, one per commit worker output).

- The commit worker's output post is now postCommitWorkerOutput, which
  closes the thread's shared transports and waits for the sidecars' exits
  before it posts the output the parent terminates on.
- runSettlementWorker closes them when its program ends, either way, before
  it reports.
- L1NodeTransport.close() also ends a sidecar that is still in its hello
  exchange, and waits for it. SidecarProcess.start is split into spawn and
  hello so the supervisor holds the child from the moment it exists. A
  failed hello now ends its child before a restart is scheduled.
- The commit worker's completion log prints byte arrays (ownerEpoch,
  generationId) as hex.

No other package spawns the sidecar from a worker thread: the watcher, the
DA committee node and the follower package start no workers, and the node's
other workers do not open the transport.

Not covered: a worker thread that ends without reaching its end path still
leaves one defunct child. That is a parent terminating it mid-run (an
interrupted commit fiber, the settlement watchdog or its scope release) and
a crashed thread. Only a sidecar owned by the main thread covers those.

Red before the fix, tests/worker-l1-sidecar-exit.test.ts, 0 passed, 4 failed:
  AssertionError: expected [ Array(5) ] to strictly equal []
  (received five "Z MainThread", the fake sidecar's process name)

Verified (rerun here):
- contrib test midgard-node, 8 files (worker-l1-sidecar-exit,
  settlement-tick-reporting, settlement-worker-supervision,
  local-node-transport.not-ready,
  prepare-hub-oracle-nonce.l1-origin-observer,
  contract-deployment-info.manifest-l1-origin.prover,
  operator-command-node-index, commit-worker-reverted-notice): 48 passed,
  0 failed.
- contrib test @al-ft/l1-node-transport: 35 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped
  (tests/devnet.test.ts needs a running devnet).
- contrib test @al-ft/midgard-l1-follower, 3 files (follow-loop.transport,
  find-origin, native-reward-account): 52 passed, 0 failed; vitest run
  tests/fork-sim/transport.test.ts: 1 passed.
- contrib mutate on close() no longer ending a starting sidecar: killed by
  the commit worker's at-once case.
- tsc --noEmit and eslint in demo/l1-node-transport, tsc --noEmit and
  eslint on the changed files in demo/midgard-node,
  check-module-size-exceptions.

Not verified:
- No devnet rerun; the defunct count on a running node was not re-measured.
- The settlement worker's success path (the test fails its program) and the
  Go sidecar binary (the tests spawn the fake sidecar).

Delete the native MPF crate's one-shot WASM path

The crate still built a wasm-bindgen package (ArchitectureGSession and
run_architecture_f over the MEF6/MEFO one-shot format) beside the
architecture-g-owner binary. Nothing loads that package: no source, script,
workflow or doc outside the crate names its exports or its
.architecture-f-wasm output directory, and no build step runs wasm-pack.

Remove the session, the one-shot engine, input parser and output encoder, and
the constants, Caps, Arena::rollback and Arena::dirty_records that only they
used. Drop the wasm-bindgen dependency, the cdylib crate type, the wasm32
cfg gates, the Makefile build target and the four ignore entries for the
generated package. The README now describes only the owner binary and keeps
the node record and event op layouts the RPC payloads refer to.

The crate's root tests ran through the one-shot engine. The two that pin
live arena behavior (an absent-key delete is refused; an empty event keeps
the root and a reinsert changes it) now call Arena::apply_event directly, the
empty-root constant test stays, and the test of the one-shot's emitted delta
is gone with it. The owner tests list a seed arena's nodes through
generated_reachable_nodes, which the owner itself uses, in place of
dirty_records.

Create each store's schema whole, shut a removed operator's node down, and drop dead labels

Schemas: no deployment exists to migrate, so every store now creates one
schema on an empty database and refuses a database created by a different
one. The node's 38 migrations, their runner and checksum ledger, the
follower's migration sets, the watcher journal migration, the db:migrate,
db:status, db:verify and db:checksum commands and the midgard-node-migrate
Compose service are removed. A refused database must be recreated.

Removed operator: a node whose operator leaves the active set reports
/readyz unready with operator_removed and then exits 0. The node's Compose
service restarts on failure only, and the process supervisor leaves a
service that exits 0 stopped. A removed operator recovers the bond and
registers again with --l1 kupmios or --l1 blockfrost. The operator-pause
drill expects the removed node to report and then exit.

Labels and docs: review, plan-phase and goal labels with no defining record
are removed from comments, test titles and messages, including the Aiken
doc comments that feed the blueprint. The network-id lifecycle snapshot is
regenerated because its transcript is seeded by the test title.
TX_VALIDATION_TABLE_ROLES.md, docs/test-quality and the testing research
note are deleted; the transaction spec's rejection section, the security
claim, the threat model and SECURITY.md name the current limits.

Lower the native owner service's module-size ceiling to 883 lines

The file shrank from 913 lines when the second promote check and the
read-wait bookkeeping were deleted.

Not verified:

Stop checking the native owner's promoted nodes twice, and delete what the node cache left behind

Promote was the larger part of a block and most of it was the node
checking the child's output again.

- The JavaScript re-hash of every promoted node is gone, with
  hashStoredNode and the golden case that pinned it. The child hashes the
  nodes and authenticates each one it is given back.
- validatePromotionClosure is deleted. The store's adopt already walks from
  the new root, refuses a node neither held nor supplied, and does not
  write a supplied node the walk does not reach.
- The record count, the unique hash order and the aggregate digest stay;
  the digest now covers the received bytes in one update.
- The ledger store reads a level's reference counts in key order.

Leftovers of the resident trie:

- Ready carries the root only; its four unused counters are gone on both
  sides.
- A restore no longer waits for in-flight diagnostics reads: it keeps the
  child, so there is no displaced child for a read to finish on. The
  diagnostics_before_request test hook goes with it.
- assertStoredNode is no longer exported.
- Comments, the readiness-reason reference, .env.example, the benchmark
  compose file and the operator message no longer speak of a sidecar, an
  index cap, or a root held "in full".

Promote, one run on each ledger with
tests/benchmarks/native-owner-node-cache.bench.ts, before and after this
commit:

  200,000 UTxOs    10,000 ops 0.9-1.3 s -> 0.74-0.86 s
                   40,000 ops 2.4-2.7 s -> 1.9-2.3 s
  1,000,000 UTxOs  10,000 ops 1.7-2.4 s -> 1.1-1.7 s
                   40,000 ops 4.7-5.6 s -> 3.5-3.8 s

What is left grows with the ledger: for every new branch the store reads
and rewrites the reference count of each child. A 256 MiB LevelDB block
cache with a 64 MiB write buffer was tried and changed nothing, so it is
not included.

Tests. "restores while a diagnostics read is in flight, and answers the
read" replaces the read-wait test: it catches diagnostics being counted as
an operation, which makes a restore refuse whenever a readiness probe is
in flight. It lives next to the other restore cases because it needs the
real child.

Verified (rerun here):
- cargo fmt --check; cargo test --release --locked: 14 passed.
- midgard-node, 31 files (mpf-native-*, native-mpf-*, mpf-differential,
  mpf-node-encoding-v1, mpf-runtime-config, readiness-native-mpf-owner-route,
  landed-blocks rebase, restore-holds and fork-sim, ledger-store-level):
  186 passed, 0 failed.
- midgard-fault-proofs ledger-store tests, 5 files: 128 passed.
- With diagnostics counted as an operation (temporary edit, undone) the new
  restore test fails with "Native MPF canonical recovery requires drained
  operations"; the other 12 cases in the file pass.
- tsc --noEmit for midgard-node and midgard-fault-proofs; eslint and
  prettier on the changed files.
- contrib boundary --package midgard-node; contrib gate process-boundaries.
- preflight: registry-paths, agent-doc-links, agent-enforcement-tags,

Not verified:
- The other test files of both packages, the devnet and the live run.
- The measurements are one run each on one machine.

Replace the native owner's resident trie with a bounded node cache

The owner child kept every node of the ledger trie in memory. The node
walked every stored node twice at start, on a child restart and whenever
the root moved back, and the child refused promotions at 2,000,000 nodes,
which was also the ledger's ceiling.

The child now keeps a cache of nodes keyed by content hash, bounded at
1 GiB (NATIVE_MPF_OWNER_NODE_CACHE_BYTES). An apply that reaches a node it
lacks answers NeedNodes; the node reads those nodes from LevelDB in one
getMany, sends them in ProvideNodes and sends the same ApplyEvents again,
for at most 66 rounds. Start, a child restart and restoreCanonicalRoot send
only the root (SetRoot); a restore keeps the same child. Applies are
serialized, since the child trims its cache when an apply ends. RPC schema
2; the binary is pinned by hash as before. Roots, the node encoding and
the LevelDB format are unchanged.

Removed: the resident index and its load messages, both walks, the sidecar
file and MPF_NATIVE_OWNER_SIDECAR_PATH, the full-index accounting, the
promotion and restore index-cap refusals with their readiness reasons
(native_mpf_promotion_index_cap_exceeded,
native_mpf_restore_index_cap_exceeded), and the owner's one-shot CLI.
Readiness diagnostics report cachedNodes and cachedBytes. A node the store
lacks under the durable root raises NativeMpfClosureIncomplete, naming it.

The promotion check no longer reads each new branch's stored children one
get at a time: the store's adopt already refuses a node neither held nor
supplied before it writes anything (ledger-store.test.ts covers it).

The L1 plan's tickets M1-M5 and benchmark B4 planned root switching,
closure import, sweeps and compaction for the resident trie; they are
replaced by a note.

Measured once per ledger, before and after, with
tests/benchmarks/native-owner-node-cache.bench.ts (added):
- 1,000,000 UTxOs: start 22-26 s -> 11-27 ms; roots of 10,000 operations
  0.13-0.18 s -> 0.16 s with the paths cached, 0.53-0.71 s first after
  start; promote of 10,000 operations 3.6-4.3 s -> 1.7-2.4 s; child memory
  after start 772 MiB -> 2 MiB, 639 MiB with every path cached.
- 200,000 UTxOs: start 4.3-4.7 s -> 13-26 ms; roots of 10,000 operations
  unchanged at 0.13 s cached, 0.45-0.69 s first after start; promote
  2.3-2.9 s -> 0.9-1.3 s.

Relay the commit program's ledger-revert notice in the emulator harness

Midgard Node CI failed on 15f60017f in
tests/deposit-flow-emulator-merge-payout.test.ts, "runs deposit, reserve
absorption, withdrawal commitment, and payout to conclusion": after the
withdrawal block rejected two transactions at commit, the validation cache
still held their outputs and lacked the input the revert restored
(tests/helpers/production-lifecycle.ts:307, the cache compared with the
spendable ledger).

A commit-stage rejection tells the cache which rows it changed through the
worker's MempoolLedgerRevertedNotice, which the parent turns into stale
marks. The emulator harness runs the commit program in process and passed
it no notifier, so the notice was never posted and nothing else names those
rows: the block that lands includes neither transaction, so the rebase's
keys do not cover them. The comparison in the lifecycle helper and the
stale marks both arrived with the validation-cache commits, and this suite
was not among the ones rerun for them.

The harness's production path now passes a notifier that hands a
MempoolLedgerRevertedNotice to the parent's dispatcher
(takeCommitWorkerOutput), so the same code marks the keys as in the node.
The other notices feed readiness, which the fixture does not follow, and
are not relayed. No source change: the node's worker already posts the
notice and its parent already marks the keys
(tests/mempool-ledger-cache.stale-marks.ts,
tests/commit-worker-reverted-notice.test.ts).

Verified (rerun here):
- Red before, same command:
  node scripts/contrib.mjs test --package midgard-node --file tests/deposit-flow-emulator-merge-payout.test.ts
  failed (2 passed, 1 failed) with the CI assertion at
  tests/helpers/production-lifecycle.ts:307.
- Green after: 3 passed in 1 file.
- Typecheck of midgard-node; eslint --max-warnings=0 and prettier on the
  two files.

Not verified:
- Which of the validation-cache commits first made the case red.
- The other emulator suites on this harness were not rerun here; the change
  acts only when a commit rejects a transaction after admission, which no
  other suite on the production path does. CI runs them all.

Claim the one-step fixture's ledger-steps module in the channel table

The one-step cross-language generator gained a second module
(generate-validation-one-step-aiken-fixture.ledger-steps.mjs) when its
ledger roots moved to a library-trie oracle. The golden channel table
still listed only the entry module, so the table's own test refused the
new file as an unclaimed generator and Agent Skills CI failed on the
branch head.

Verified (rerun here):
- Red before, the workflow's command
  (node --test over every .agents/skills/*/scripts/*.test.mjs):
  210 tests, 1 failed, "PROBLEM: demo/midgard-validation/scripts/
  generate-validation-one-step-aiken-fixture.ledger-steps.mjs looks like a
  generator but no channel claims it (add it to channels.json)".
- Green after, same command: 210 tests, 210 passed.
- node scripts/ci/check-agent-skills.mjs exits 0; its own test passes 8 of 8.
